title: Outage-minimizing maintenance scheduler with burst leases
creator: Ravi Shah
description: A scheduler that minimizes application outages during planned maintenance by coordinating node drains, short-term burst leases, and autoscaler hints. This ticket defines the design and rollout of a system that: 1) creates short-lived 'burst leases' to temporarily increase capacity during drains, 2) reserves throughput tokens against customer contracts to guarantee SLOs during maintenance, and 3) integrates with the autoscaler to pre-warm and gracefully decommission nodes while preserving KV caches where possible.
background: Customers on Dedicated capacity reported brief SLO violations during rolling upgrades and maintenance windows where autoscaler ramp-up lagged behind drain-induced load shifts. Existing approaches (staggered drains, tokenized reservations) mitigate some cases but do not coordinate prewarming, temporary burst pool allocation, and per-customer throughput reservations simultaneously. This proposal aims to unify those controls to reduce P99 latency spikes and request shedding during maintenance.
goals: 1) Reduce maintenance-related P99 latency regressions by >=60% compared to baseline. 2) Eliminate request shedding for high-priority reserved customers during planned drains. 3) Provide a gradual rollout path with feature flags and canary groups. 4) Keep added cost of burst leases to <10% of monthly Dedicated spend for typical rolling upgrades.
non_goals: 1) Address unscheduled node failures or hardware preemption (handled by existing fallback policies). 2) Replace longer-term capacity planning and reservations—this is a temporary mitigation for maintenance windows.
design_decisions: 1) Introduce a lease manager that issues time-limited burst leases tied to maintenance tickets. 2) Each lease consumes from a per-tenant throughput token bucket; tokens can be purchased via committed capacity or consumed from a global maintenance buffer for emergency windows. 3) Autoscaler will accept 'prewarm' hints with a time-to-ready estimate; prewarmed nodes are placed in a separate ready pool that respects tenant isolation. 4) Drains will include 'safety windows' during which the scheduler avoids moving hot KV caches unless lease capacity is available. 5) Feature toggles at tenant and fleet levels to disable leases or use conservative draining.
algorithm_overview: - Maintenance ticket created -> scheduler computes affected shards and expected traffic shift. - Scheduler requests burst capacity from burst pool; if available, issues leases per tenant with throughput targets. - Autoscaler prewarms N nodes (heuristic uses historical peak and current inflight). - Begin rolling drains with staggered drains and KV-preservation attempts; if drain causes latency > threshold, scheduler extends leases or scales burst pool. - On completion, leases expire and prewarmed nodes are absorbed back or decommissioned based on autoscaler policy.
acceptance_criteria: Canary rollout to 5% of fleets shows no >1% increase in cost and P99 latency improvement >= 40% for maintenance events.
System issues leases and honors per-tenant throughput reservations during scheduled drains for test tenants in canary.
Automated chaos test (simulated scheduled drains + sudden 30% traffic spike) does not trigger request shedding for reserved tenants.
Dashboard surfaces lease utilization, tokens consumed, prewarm latency, and maintenance-induced SLO delta.
implementation_tasks: Write lease manager service and API (ownership: runtime/ops).
Integrate lease issuance into maintenance ticket workflow and Console UI.
Add autoscaler prewarm API and implement heuristic for prewarm sizing.
Modify drain controller to consult lease manager and KV-preservation hints.
Instrument telemetry: lease metrics, token balance per-tenant, prewarm success rate, maintenance event latency deltas.
End-to-end tests: unit, integration, and synthetic load harness for scheduled drain scenarios.
Create Console controls and rollout feature flag by tenant and by fleet.
Documentation: PRD, runbook for on-call, and user docs explaining cost/behavior of burst leases.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Unit and integration tests in staging + feature flag off (2 weeks). Phase 2: Internal canary on platform teams and dedicated test tenants (1 week). Phase 3: 5% customer canary with monitoring and runbook ready (2 weeks). Phase 4: Gradual ramp to 25% then GA after meeting SLA/metrics gates. Emergency kill switch and automatic rollback if token exhaustion or unexpected shedding is detected.
risks: Burst leases increase monthly cost if left enabled indiscriminately — mitigated by per-tenant caps and chargeback.
Token accounting complexity for customers spanning multiple fleets — mitigate with centralized ledger and reconciliation job.
Prewarm mis-sizing could waste GPUs or be insufficient; iteration required on heuristics.
Complexity in KV-preservation logic may increase drain duration; balance with customer SLOs in scheduler policies.
mitigations: Default conservative caps and opt-in for non-committed tenants.
Visibility: Console shows projected cost of upcoming maintenance leases before issuance.
Start with fleets that have predictable load patterns and non-heterogeneous models.
Run synthetic load tests and tune prewarm heuristics before customer canaries.
security_and_compliance_notes: No new customer data is introduced. Ledger and token accounting will follow existing KMS/HSM patterns. Ensure audit logs for lease issuance and token consumption are retained per Console retention policy.
